knowledge:
- key_parameters: MARGIN=1 or 2 in summary() and assayDataApply() to specify feature-wise (1) or sample-wise (2) operations ;; GROUP in summary() or esBy() to summarize or split data by sample annotation groups ;; log2=TRUE/FALSE in summary() to toggle between log2-based geometric statistics and raw arithmetic statistics ;; type in normalize() to specify the normalization method (e.g., "nSolver") ;; fromELT and toELT in normalize() to define the source and target assayData elements ;; qcCutoffs in setQCFlags() to set custom thresholds for Housekeeper, Imaging, BindingDensity, ERCCLinearity, and ERCCLoD ;; type in autoplot() to specify the plot type (e.g., "heatmap-genes", "housekeep-geom", "lane-bindingDensity", "lane-fov", "ercc-linearity", "ercc-lod", "boxplot-feature")
- alternatives: None mentioned; the package extends Biobase's ExpressionSet and provides specialized methods for NanoString-specific data structures.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing transcriptomics data generated from the NanoString nCounter platform, starting from raw RCC count files, an RLF panel design file, and a sample annotation CSV.
- pitfalls: Samples with low housekeeper signal (geometric mean below 32 counts) must be excluded, while those between 32 and 100 are "borderline" and should be treated with caution ;; Binding density must fall within specific ranges (0.1 - 2.25 for MAX/FLEX, 0.1 - 1.8 for SPRINT) to avoid probe overlap issues ;; At least 75% of fields of view (FOVs) must be successfully counted for robust imaging QC ;; ERCC linearity correlation values below 0.95 indicate hybridization or assay performance issues.

workflows.name: nanostring_ncounter_analysis
workflows.intent: Read raw NanoString RCC/RLF files, perform quality control, normalize counts, and visualize results.
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw RCC, RLF, and sample annotation files into a NanoStringRCCSet object using readNanoStringRccSet ;; 2. Assign design information and adjust dimension labels ;; 3. Perform quality control flagging using setQCFlags and visualize QC metrics (housekeeper genes, binding density, imaging FOV, ERCC linearity, and ERCC LOD) using autoplot ;; 4. Subset the data to remove low-quality samples or focus on specific subsets (e.g., endogenous genes) using subset or endogenousSubset ;; 5. Normalize the expression data using normalize (e.g., "nSolver" method) ;; 6. Transform and export data using munge or transform, and visualize normalized expression using autoplot heatmaps.
workflows.code:
demoData <- readNanoStringRccSet(rcc_files, rlfFile = rlf_file, phenoDataFile = sample_annotation)
design(demoData) <- ~ `Treatment`
protocolData(demoData)[["Sample ID"]] <- sampleNames(demoData)
dimLabels(demoData)[2] <- "Sample ID"
demoData <- setQCFlags(demoData,
                       qcCutoffs = list(Housekeeper = c(failingCutoff = 32, passingCutoff = 100), 
                                        Imaging = c(fovCutoff = 0.75), 
                                        BindingDensity = c(minimumBD = 0.1, maximumBD = 2.25, maximumBDSprint = 1.8), 
                                        ERCCLinearity = c(correlationValue = 0.95), 
                                        ERCCLoD = c(standardDeviations = 2)))
girafe(ggobj = autoplot(demoData, type = "housekeep-geom"))
girafe(ggobj = autoplot(demoData, type = "lane-bindingDensity"))
girafe(ggobj = autoplot(demoData, type = "lane-fov"))
girafe(ggobj = autoplot(demoData, type = "ercc-linearity"))
demoData <- normalize(demoData, type="nSolver", fromELT = "exprs", toELT = "exprs_norm")
autoplot(demoData, type = "heatmap-genes", elt = "exprs_norm", heatmapGroup = c("Treatment", "BRAFGenotype"), 
         show_colnames_gene_limit = 10, show_rownames_gene_limit = 40,
         log2scale = FALSE)
neg_ctrls <- munge(neg_set, ~exprs)
exprs_df <- transform(assayData(demoData)[["exprs_norm"]])
